source.title: SAE features for refusal and sycophancy steering vectors
source.authors: neverix; Dmitrii Kharlapenko; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: The full post is present. Referenced charts are not included with readable values in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The post evaluates refusal-related residual-stream vector ablations and SAE reconstructions using a direction-estimation method different from the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation method in V1.
record.gate_note: The post also reports an SAE feature accuracy result on MMLU and unsuccessful sycophancy-vector reconstructions on Gemma, but these do not test the claim versions about refusal. Descriptions of charts are included without readable chart values.
record.test_reason: The post ablates a refusal direction and its SAE reconstructions from all residual-stream layers of Phi-3 Mini, a model not in the original paper. It reports qualitatively, via figures, the effect on JailbreakBench refusal and safety and on MMLU. The direction comes from an SVD of the weight difference between Phi-3 and a released abliterated Phi-3, not directly from difference-in-means. The main aim is to evaluate SAEs, so this is a weak, figure-only test of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE reconstructions of a refusal direction (2–4 features, best at k=4) match or surpass the original vector, approach an optimized skyline, and keep MMLU. They caution the result may not be robust, citing the questionable SVD-derived vector, one judge, and 100 samples. The 'two features' framing should note that k=4 performed best overall.
record.recipe_differences: Follows the cited refusal-direction ablation approach, but estimates the direction from an SVD of the difference between the first MLP weight matrices of base and abliterated models, then reconstructs it with SAE features. The post says this estimate is questionable.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that k=4 performs better overall than k=3, although k=3 is closest to the target vector by distance; their best reconstructions use layer-16 SAEs from the sixth residual-SAE group.
record.problems: The authors say the original vector estimate may not be robust, the results are from one model and 100 samples, and the safety score uses one LLaMA Guard judge. The supplied text does not expose the chart values, and no control comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional readable result values were available in the referenced charts. The k=3 vector's distance advantage is a selection/comparison detail, not a separate reported behavioral outcome; other figure-only points are not individually extractable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction is not systematically tested; there is only an anecdote that large scales make Self-Explanation requests get refused. Only one model has readable claims, and the Gemma refusal analysis has no stated outcome.
A released abliterated Phi-3 is used only as a source for the direction. Its own refusal rate is not reported in the text.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training is tested.
A multi-feature SAE reconstruction of one vector does not test whether refusal spans multiple directions.
The Gemma 1 analysis is mentioned with no refusal outcome.
Not addressed. The Appendix B remark that LaMini models lack refusal is an observation, not a direction test.

missing.what: Ablation result for the original SVD-derived direction itself, and for the finetuned skyline vector, on JailbreakBench refusal and safety
Anecdote that adding the direction at large scales makes the model refuse the Self-Explanation request (induction direction of V1)
Harmful minus harmless difference of mean SAE encodings recovers the same two refusal-related features (39432, 5382) as ITO
Gemma 1 layer-12 refusal analysis, mentioned with no reported outcome

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's limits_scope label. The caveats it cited (recipe deviation, one judge, 100 samples) are robustness concerns about the study, not conditions where V1 fails. The dependence on feature count concerns the SAE reconstruction, not V1. The sycophancy, MMLU-classifier and MELBO results do not bear on refusal-direction versions.

versions.untested_parts: The direction was estimated from a weight-matrix difference, not the stated harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation difference. The post reports removal/ablation results, not inducing refusals on harmless requests by adding the direction.
The post uses released abliterated weights to estimate a direction; it does not report testing a weight edit that removes refusal.
No jailbreak attack is tested as suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is tested.
Representing a vector with multiple SAE features does not test whether refusal itself is better described by multiple directions, an affine structure, or a cone.
The post does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
A Gemma analysis is mentioned, but no outcome on refusal-direction transfer is stated.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

relationships.condition: Phi-3 Mini, ablation of an SVD-derived refusal direction and its 2–4 feature SAE reconstructions, JailbreakBench (100 samples), LLaMA Guard 2 judge
relationships.reason: The text states that ablating the reconstructed directions reduces refusal to near the optimized skyline while keeping MMLU (r1, r2, r3). This is qualitative only, because chart values are not readable.
relationships.display_finding: Ablating reconstructions using 2–4 SAE features reduced refusal to near the optimized reference while retaining MMLU performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe the reconstructed directions as improving or preserving refusal-related performance while not sacrificing MMLU performance (r1–r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The text cautions that the result uses one model and 100 samples with one safety judge, and that its original direction was derived from a weight-matrix SVD rather than the stated difference-in-means procedure (r1–r3).
